Every choice matters—even the quiet ones. Downtime gives players time to prepare, craft, build, or reflect. But time alone doesnʼt guarantee results. This section provides mechanical support for tracking progress, resolving tasks, and introducing narrative tension through risk and opportunity.

Many downtime tasks cost: •Materials ( 🪵 ): Needed for crafting, repairs, construction •Energy ( ⚡ ): Powers advanced base actions •Herbs ( 🌿 ): Used in potion making or ritual research •Food ( 🍞 ): Required for homestead labor and feasts Let players track usage or automate it via facilities and staff (see Base/Homesteading rules). 💤 Fatigue from Overexertion If a character skips rest to gain extra downtime hours: •1st Day: No penalty •2nd Day: Gain Fatigue Level 1 (disadvantage on physical checks) •3rd Day+: +1 Fatigue per day; risk exhaustion or mental strain •Recovery: One full rest day = remove 1 level of fatigue Certain archetypes, species, or cybernetic upgrades may reduce fatigue buildup.

Some Homestead Events (see Section 8) affect outdoor facilities directly. During each Base Turn, GMs may: •Roll once per homestead •Roll once per 3–4 outdoor facilities •Or resolve events monthly (for seasonal pacing)

Seasons Shift. Winds Howl. Even the Land Has Stories. Homesteads are alive—shaped by nature, weather, creatures, and unknown forces across the multiverse. Each Base Turn or season, the GM may roll a Homestead Event, representing the dynamic challenges and opportunities that outdoor systems must endure. Events can: •Reward strategic planning or upgrades •Disrupt or threaten food and energy production •Introduce plot hooks, local rumors, or interdimensional consequences •Reflect environmental or planar traits (e.g., fire moons, swamp worlds, starless wastes)

•Space: Each facility requires a number of Land Plots. Most need 1–2. •Staffing: Unstaffed facilities may function at reduced output or shut down. •Orders: Facilities receive 1 order per Base Turn. When currency isnʼt viable or the buyer wants to trade, players may use bartering.
Whenever a character tries to buy or sell goods, they may negotiate for a better deal. Use the following rules to adjust prices:

Characters can use downtime to improve returns or reduce risk: •Market Monitoring (DC 12 Intelligence/Insight): ◦ Success: Reroll investment performance this month. •Hands-On Involvement (DC 15 Persuasion/Business): ◦ Success: Raise return by 5% or reduce loss chance.

Players managing trade or investment during downtime may roll to optimize profits: •Market Research: Intelligence (Investigation) DC 12 ◦ Success: Advantage on next negotiation or pricing roll. •Connection Maintenance: Charisma (Persuasion) DC 10 ◦ Success: Prevents price increases or service interruptions. •Trade Oversight: Wisdom (Insight) DC 12 ◦ Success: +5% bonus to this periodʼs profit from that trade activity. These rules provide a flexible and modular way to handle trade, whether you want a simple side hustle or a full-blown economic empire. Use only the parts that match your groupʼs playstyle.
Roll a 1d20 to determine change in share value: Players may sell at any time, but they must sell all shares in one transaction unless otherwise stated.
